indicators.note: one thing sitting in another means it is placed inside it

parts.note: ace is slang for excellent or fabulous
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A runner sprinting through some wonderful stretch of land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run' looks like the action of the surface, but it is the cricket abbreviation; ace is informal for excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: An acre is a unit of land measurement, so it names a specific extent of ground.

clue.text: Wild horse, breed mostly seen around North Carolina

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
to be seen around something is to surround it, so one part wraps the other

parts.note: to brood is to breed or hatch young; its last letter goes
NC is the US postal code for the state, its two initials

explanation.surface: A wild horse being bred on a ranch in North Carolina.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breed' must be read as a verb for its synonym brood; 'mostly' trims that synonym before the state goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A bronco is an untamed or half-broken horse of the American West, famous from rodeo riding.

clue.text: Concerned with valuable clothing? This will get oil out

parts.note: re means regarding or concerning, as in a letter heading
finery is showy, expensive dress

explanation.surface: Someone fretting about an oil stain on their best clothes and looking for a cleaner.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests stain removal from fine garments; the definition is really about an industrial plant processing crude.
explanation.definitionFit: A refinery is the plant where crude petroleum is processed and its usable products are separated.

clue.text: Skin disease found in seven cases retrospectively

indicators.note: looking back in time suggests reading backwards
something found in a phrase is tucked inside its letters

parts.note: the letters spanning the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A doctor reviewing seven case histories of a skin complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: sevEN CAses holds ENCA, which read backwards gives ACNE.
explanation.definitionFit: Acne is a common inflammatory skin condition producing pimples, especially in teenagers.

parts.note: a prop is a support
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the late Queen Elizabeth II

explanation.surface: Backing the old monarch because it seems the right thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is the royal cipher of Elizabeth II, hence 'former queen'.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper and appropriate are synonyms, both meaning suitable or fitting for the situation.

parts.note: a den is a private room for reading or work
an ounce is a small unit of weight

explanation.surface: Dismissing a piece of research as carrying hardly any weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Study' reads as research, but it is the room.
explanation.definitionFit: To denounce is to criticise publicly and strongly, the same as to condemn.

clue.text: Seldom met with Mark before church

parts.note: a scar is a mark left on the skin
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone rarely meeting their friend Mark ahead of the Sunday service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a man's name but is a blemish; the definition swallows the 'met with' that seems to belong to Mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Something scarce is rarely encountered because there is little of it about.

parts.note: a coach is a railway carriage, a car
a teacher's pet is a favourite

explanation.surface: A sports coach scolded for sticking by a favoured player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' sounds like a trainer, but here it is a rail carriage. To carpet someone is British informal for calling them in to be told off.
explanation.definitionFit: To carpet someone is an idiom for summoning and scolding them, from being called onto the boss's carpet.

clue.text: Intervening period led to EMI going west

parts.note: if one thing led to another it meant it as a consequence

indicators.note: in an across entry, heading west is moving right to left, so letters run backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A gap in a band's career before their record label EMI moved operations westward.
explanation.walkthrough: EMI is the record company; 'going west' also suggests failing, but here it just turns the letters round.
explanation.definitionFit: The meantime is the interval between two events, the time in between.

indicators.note: turning something round makes it face the other way

parts.note: a loop is a circle

explanation.surface: A circle of players around a game in the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circle round' reads as a single phrase, but the second word works on the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Pool is a cue game played on a pocketed table, a fixture in many bars.

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so only each word's closing letter counts

parts.note: the closing letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: A performer being told to sing into the main mic at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally' applies to both 'main' and 'microphone', not just the second.
explanation.definitionFit: To intone is to chant or recite in a sustained musical voice, a form of singing.

clue.text: Part of air in mobile ringtone

indicators.note: mobile means able to move, so the letters move about

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A snatch of a tune heard in a phone's ringtone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Air' poses as a tune and 'mobile' as a phone; the definition is chemical.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitrogen gas makes up about four fifths of the atmosphere we breathe.

parts.note: to sire is to father; a sire is a male parent
N is the standard abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A dad being introduced to a dangerous seductress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Father' is a verb-noun for a male parent, especially of a horse; N for new is a standard abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A siren is a beautiful, dangerously alluring woman, named after the mythical singers who lured sailors.

clue.text: Check back of car concealed by street corner

indicators.note: to be concealed by something is to be covered and enclosed by it

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of the word
a corner is an angle

explanation.surface: Inspecting the rear of a car hidden around a street corner.
explanation.walkthrough: R is enclosed by STANGLE, the street abbreviation followed by the corner.
explanation.definitionFit: To strangle growth or a sound is to suppress or restrain it, one sense of check.

indicators.note: in means inside, so the letters sit within a word

parts.note: the middle letters of the word

explanation.surface: Admitting that, honestly, one's life is dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In truth' reads as 'honestly', but it is a hiding place.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a rut means living a dull, unchanging routine one cannot escape.

parts.note: Tango is T in the NATO phonetic alphabet
an ally is a partner

explanation.surface: Keeping in touch with one's dance partner from tango classes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tango partner' reads as a dancer, but tango only supplies its letter.
explanation.definitionFit: When two accounts tally they agree or match, which is to correspond.

clue.text: Clingy individual allowed to hold naughty child

indicators.note: holding something means enclosing it, so one part wraps the other

parts.note: let means allowed
an imp is a mischievous child

explanation.surface: A needy person permitted to look after a badly behaved youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clingy individual' is figurative: the definition is a sea creature used as a metaphor for a hanger-on.
explanation.definitionFit: A limpet is a shellfish that clings hard to rocks, so figuratively someone who will not let go.

clue.text: What's cutting criminal charge — that is right

parts.note: a rap is a criminal charge, as in beating the rap
i.e. is the abbreviation for 'that is'
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Asking which part of a criminal charge is being dropped, and agreeing it is correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What's cutting' looks like a question about reductions; it describes a blade.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapier is a slender sword, a weapon with a cutting and thrusting edge.

indicators.note: in a down entry, what supports something sits underneath it, so that piece goes second

parts.note: the plane is a broad-leaved tree common in city streets
T is the abbreviation for tons

explanation.surface: Tonnes of soil holding up a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, a piece supporting another sits beneath it, so T comes last. 'Earth' looks like soil but is our world.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth is an example of the class: it is the third world orbiting the Sun.

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came

parts.note: a mood is the atmosphere or feeling of a place

explanation.surface: Coming home to find the atmosphere spoilt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Atmosphere' suggests air or weather, but here it is the feeling in a room.
explanation.definitionFit: Doom means destruction or a dreadful fate, the same as ruin.

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the US Department of Defense building in Arlington, Virginia

explanation.walkthrough: SHAPE in capitals looks like the NATO acronym for Supreme Headquarters Allied Powers Europe, which makes the whole clue read as one military definition; it is just a shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A pentagon is a five-sided polygon, and the five-sided American defence building is named after that form.

clue.text: Cause for regret is mine over years

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
Y is the abbreviation for years

explanation.surface: Someone lamenting a sorrow that has been theirs for years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mine' looks like a possessive but is a pit; in a down entry, over means placed above.
explanation.definitionFit: A pity is something unfortunate that one is sorry about, as in 'it's a pity'.

indicators.note: what is carried is held inside the carrier

parts.note: a ring is round, shaped like the letter O
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: A jewelled ring being brought along by a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: The ring sits at the very front of PAL, a container with nothing before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Opal is a precious stone known for its shifting play of colours.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an arid region, the Kalahari being one in southern Africa
second meaning: to abandon or betray, as in ratting on someone

explanation.walkthrough: 'Kalahari rat' sounds like a desert rodent; 'rat' is really a verb for leaving one's side.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kalahari is an example of an arid wilderness, and to rat on people is to abandon them.

indicators.note: what follows comes after, so the piece named first is placed second

parts.note: the lee is the side sheltered from the wind
a way is a path

explanation.surface: A footpath running alongside a protected edge of land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' puts the path after the sheltered side, though it comes first in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeway is extra room or allowance for error, a margin to work within.
